description: Imports Google Ads accounts, campaigns, ad groups, ads, labels and performance/geo/keyword/click reports for one or more customer IDs via GAQL.

transports.purpose: All data access goes through the vendor `google-ads` Python client library (gRPC), not through hand-rolled HTTP calls. See unionMisfits[0].

spec.apiVersionPinning: Hard-coded API version constant `v25`, passed to GoogleAdsClient.load_from_dict(version=...) and used for the generated proto/type imports. Not a header/path/query the connector controls.

credentialModes.name: Google OAuth2 refresh token + Google Ads developer token

continuity.ourSideLoss: `click_view` is capped by `days_of_data_storage = 90`: the slice generator clamps the start date to now-(90 - conversion_window) days, so any click_view day older than that window can never be fetched again. Other streams are re-queryable from `start_date` at any time.
continuity.resumeWindow: ~90 days minus conversion_window_days for click_view; effectively unbounded for every other stream. Separately, an individual in-flight page token expires after roughly 2 hours (the connector chunks slices to 15 days for exactly this reason) — but that only affects a single running sweep, not a pause between runs.
continuity.notes: Read-only GAQL queries; the connector creates nothing server-side on the customer's Google Ads account. Cursor state is a per-customer-id `segments.date` date string held in Flow state, so a pause costs nothing except click_view retention.

configFields.name: credentials.client_secret
configFields.description: Client Secret of the Google Ads developer OAuth application.

configFields.name: credentials.refresh_token

configFields.name: credentials.developer_token
configFields.description: Google Ads API developer token. Marked 'Injected by Flow' in the spec and populated from the OAuth server output specification, but the underlying google-ads client requires it; a standalone deployment must supply one obtained through Google's separate developer-token approval process.

configFields.name: customer_id
configFields.description: Comma-separated list of 10-digit customer IDs (pattern ^[0-9]{10}(,[0-9]{10})*$). Each becomes a stream slice.

configFields.name: end_date
configFields.description: YYYY-MM-DD ceiling; min(today, end_date) is used.

configFields.name: custom_queries
configFields.description: List of { query, table_name, primary_key }; each becomes an additional stream.

configFields.name: custom_queries[].query
configFields.description: GAQL text; parsed and validated by a regex GAQL parser. Must not contain segments.date when the stream is to be incremental — the connector injects that predicate itself.

configFields.name: custom_queries[].primary_key
configFields.description: Comma-delimited field list; whether it contains segments.date decides incremental vs full refresh.

configFields.name: login_customer_id
configFields.displayName: Login Customer ID for Managed Accounts
configFields.description: Manager (MCC) account ID; passed straight into the google-ads client credentials dict.

configFields.name: conversion_window_days
configFields.description: 0..1095, default 14. Cursor is rewound by this many days on every slice generation to catch late conversions.

configFields.name: stream
configFields.description: Name of the Airbyte stream to capture (from the estuary-cdk airbyte shim ResourceConfig).

configFields.name: cursorField
configFields.description: Discovered bindings emit ["segments.date"] for incremental streams.

configFields.name: namespace
configFields.description: Unused by this connector; part of the shared shim ResourceConfig.

discovery.method: Static class list in source.py `streams()`, filtered at runtime by an account probe, plus user-declared custom GAQL queries whose column types are resolved through GoogleAdsFieldService.
discovery.querySketch: Account probe: the internal ServiceAccounts stream runs `SELECT <customer schema fields> FROM customer` once per configured customer_id to learn customer.id / customer.time_zone / customer.manager. Accounts with customer.manager = true are excluded from every metrics stream. For custom queries: `SELECT name, data_type, enum_values, is_repeated WHERE name IN (<fields>)` against GoogleAdsFieldService, and `SELECT name, selectable_with WHERE name = 'segments.date'` to decide whether the query's resource can be incremental at all.
excludes: service_accounts (internal service class; documented as 'not exposed to a user' and never returned by streams())

campaigns, user_location_report, account_performance_report, display_topics_performance_report, display_keyword_performance_report, shopping_performance_report, ad_group_ad_report, geographic_report, keyword_report — all omitted entirely when every configured customer is a manager account
custom queries containing metrics.* fields when there are no non-manager accounts
discovery.allowlist: REPORT_MAPPING in google_ads.py is the fixed stream-name -> GAQL resource table; only names present there can be built from a shipped JSON schema.

incremental.querySketch: GAQL: SELECT <all properties of schemas/accounts.json> FROM customer WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC — issued once per customer_id per 15-day slice; slice start is rewound by conversion_window_days.
GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM campaign WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC. Non-manager customers only.

snapshot.querySketch: GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM campaign_label — no WHERE/ORDER BY clause is appended when there is no cursor field; re-read in full per customer_id each run.

incremental.querySketch: GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM ad_group WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC.
GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM ad_group_ad WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC.
GAQL: SELECT <schema fields incl. metrics.*> FROM customer WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC. Non-manager customers only.

GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM topic_view WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC. Non-manager customers only.
GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM shopping_performance_view WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC. Non-manager customers only.
GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM user_location_view WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC. Non-manager customers only.
GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM geographic_view WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC. Non-manager customers only.
GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM keyword_view WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date <= '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC. Non-manager customers only.

GAQL: SELECT <schema fields> FROM click_view WHERE segments.date >= '{slice_start}' AND segments.date < '{slice_end}' ORDER BY segments.date ASC. Unlike every other stream this one uses range_days = 1 (one day per slice) and days_of_data_storage = 90, which clamps the slice start to now-(90 - conversion_window_days).

The user's own GAQL, re-parsed and rewritten: segments.date is appended to the SELECT list if absent, and `segments.date BETWEEN '{slice_start}' AND '{slice_end}'` is ANDed onto any existing WHERE clause. Chosen when the query's resource is selectable_with segments.date AND the declared primary_key contains segments.date.

snapshot.querySketch: The user's GAQL emitted verbatim (after regex normalisation), once per customer_id. Chosen when the query's resource is not selectable_with segments.date, or when the declared primary_key omits segments.date.

authTierRationale: The spec declares exactly one credential object and marks client_id, client_secret and refresh_token all as required — there is no API-key or service-account alternative anywhere in the code. The connector hands that dict straight to GoogleAdsClient.load_from_dict, which additionally needs a developer_token. Standalone, therefore, the user must (a) register their own Google Cloud OAuth client, (b) run the adwords-scoped consent flow themselves to obtain a refresh token, and (c) separately apply to Google for a Google Ads API developer token — an out-of-band human approval process that is not self-serve and can take days. Estuary's hosted control plane softens (a) and (c): the OAuth2Spec in __main__.py registers a Google provider flow, and the spec's complete_oauth_server_output_specification writes client_id, client_secret AND developer_token into the connector config (the developer_token field is literally described as 'Injected by Flow'), so a hosted user only clicks through Google consent. That hosted convenience does not change the standalone tier, which is T3.

unionMisfits.description: This connector speaks no HTTP that it controls. Every read goes through the vendor `google-ads` Python client over gRPC: GoogleAdsClient.load_from_dict(credentials, version='v25'), then client.get_service('GoogleAdsService').search(SearchGoogleAdsRequest). There is no base URL, no path, no header set and no query string in the connector source, so none of http/sql/objectStore/stream fits. I emitted a non-union `vendorSdk` spec rather than inventing endpoint paths.

Paginator has no honest value here. `ga_service.search()` returns a google.api_core SearchPager which walks next_page_token internally; the connector merely iterates it. The only pagination evidence in connector code is negative: a DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 1000 class constant that is never referenced, and EXPIRED_PAGE_TOKEN error handling that retries a slice from the last-seen cursor value. Recording a paginator would be a guess about library internals.

There is no separate backfill leg. One code path (chunk_date_range + a per-customer segments.date cursor) produces both the historical sweep and the ongoing one: it walks 15-day windows from `start_date` (or the stored cursor) to now, and every run rewinds the cursor by conversion_window_days so recent windows are re-read forever. The schema's backfill/incremental split forces a choice; I put the single shape in `incremental` and left `backfill` null.

No schedule of any kind exists in this connector or in the airbyte shim's ResourceConfig (which carries only stream / syncMode / namespace / cursorField). Cadence is entirely the Flow runtime's business. Empty lists here mean 'absent', not 'continuous'.

The two custom-query archetypes are neither 'static' (they do not exist unless the user writes GAQL into custom_queries) nor 'discovered' in the schema's sense (they come from connector config, not from the customer's own schema). Their *column types*, however, genuinely are discovered at connect time via GoogleAdsFieldService. I marked them origin 'discovered' as the lesser distortion.

Full-refresh streams (campaign_labels, ad_group_labels, ad_group_ad_labels, geo_target_constant) re-read the entire resource every run and re-emit keyed documents. That upserts by key but never deletes: a label removed in Google Ads persists in the collection forever. It is not 'snapshot_with_tombstone' (no tombstones are emitted) and calling it 'merge' hides the staleness. Same applies to hard-deleted campaigns/ads on the incremental streams.

`service_accounts` has a shipped JSON schema and a REPORT_MAPPING entry but is deliberately never exposed — its docstring says 'intended to be used as a service class, not exposed to a user' and streams() never returns it. It is used once per run to resolve customer time zones and manager flags. Omitted from the stream list; noting it so a reader who greps the schemas directory does not think a stream is missing.

Nine of the eighteen streams are constructed only when at least one configured customer is a non-manager account, and the customer list itself is split (manager-safe streams get all customers, metrics streams get non-managers only). The schema has no way to express 'this stream exists only under condition X on the customer's account topology'.

abstained.transports[0].spec.baseUrl: The connector never names a host. GoogleAdsClient resolves the endpoint internally (and honours an endpoint override the connector does not set). Writing googleads.googleapis.com would be recall, not extraction.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: Headers (developer-token, login-customer-id, authorization) are assembled by the google-ads library from the credentials dict; the connector sets none itself. login_customer_id is merely copied into that dict.
abstained.streams[*].pull.*.paginator: Pagination is entirely inside google.api_core's SearchPager. The one page-size constant in connector code (GoogleAds.DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE = 1000) is dead — grep finds no reader. See unionMisfits[1].
abstained.streams[*].schedules: No cadence is expressed anywhere in the connector or in the airbyte shim's ResourceConfig.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: Same: scheduling belongs to the Flow runtime, not this connector.
abstained.execution.continuity.releasedOnShutdown: Not applicable in a way the code decides — no server-side artifact is created, so there is nothing to release; recording `false` would imply artifacts exist.
abstained.streams[*].supportedSyncModes for full-r: GoogleAdsStream subclasses have no cursor at all, so incremental is impossible for them; the discover snapshot confirms syncMode full_refresh. Recorded as fact, not abstained — noting here only that the *shipped* discover output, not a code branch, is the corroborating source.
abstained.streams[].name for custom queries: Custom-query stream names are whatever the user types into custom_queries[].table_name (the test fixture uses 'my_custom_query'). Emitted as archetypes with placeholder names rather than inventing a concrete list.
